issues.legal_issue: Incorrect valuation of a suit or deficient court fees do not, by themselves, negate good faith in prosecuting the suit in a court later found to lack jurisdiction, where the plaintiff acted diligently and promptly presented the plaint to the proper court.
material_facts: The plaintiffs filed two suits for possession in a court that later ordered the plaints returned because it lacked jurisdiction.
The plaintiffs presented the returned plaints in the proper court on the same day they received them.
The suits had been incorrectly valued and the court fees had been calculated on that valuation.
The defendants argued that the suits were time-barred, and the High Court held that the valuation and court-fee errors showed a lack of good faith.
issues.conclusion: The valuation and court-fee errors did not establish a lack of good faith. The plaintiffs were entitled to the benefit of excluding the time spent prosecuting the suits in the court that lacked jurisdiction, and the suits were not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the Limitation Act provides for exclusion of time spent prosecuting with due diligence and in good faith another civil proceeding concerning the same matter against the same defendant in a court unable to entertain it because of a jurisdictional defect. Good faith qualifies the prosecution of the proceeding in that court. An error in valuing the suit or a failure to pay the requisite court fee does not, by itself, bear on that good faith. The Court relied on Section 14 and cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: civil_suit_with_limitation_defense and same_matter_prosecuted_in_first_court and first_court_unable_to_entertain_for_jurisdiction_defect and plaintiffs_prosecuted_first_case_diligently_and_in_good_faith and plaintiffs_promptly_represented_returned_plaint

predicates.civil_suit_with_limitation_defense: A defendant in a civil suit contended that the suit was filed outside the applicable limitation period.
predicates.same_matter_prosecuted_in_first_court: The plaintiffs pursued an earlier civil proceeding against the defendant concerning the same matter.
predicates.first_court_unable_to_entertain_for_juri: The first court could not entertain the proceeding because of a defect in its jurisdiction.
predicates.plaintiffs_prosecuted_first_case_diligen: The plaintiffs diligently and honestly pursued the proceeding in the first court.
predicates.plaintiffs_promptly_represented_returned: After the first court returned the plaint, the plaintiffs promptly presented it to the proper court.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_time_excluded_from_li: The time spent prosecuting the earlier proceeding is left out when calculating limitation.

issues.definition: When plaintiffs diligently and in good faith pursue the same civil matter in a court unable to entertain it for a jurisdictional defect, and promptly present the returned plaint to the proper court, the time spent in the earlier proceeding is excluded from the limitation calculation.
